name: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS / BASS-II)
facility: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / BASS Flow Duct
lead_investigators: Paul V. Ferkul (NCSER / Case Western Reserve University)
Sandra L. Olson (NASA Glenn Research Center)
James S. T'ien (Case Western Reserve University)
description: BASS investigated the combustion and extinction limits of solid polymeric materials (flat polymethyl methacrylate PMMA slabs, cylindrical PMMA rods, and cotton-fiberglass fabrics) in microgravity aboard the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox. Experiments evaluated concurrent and opposed flow flame spread velocities, stand-off distances, and extinguishment via flow cessation and nitrogen (N2) dilution, providing direct microgravity validation data for NASA-STD-6001 spacecraft flammability standards.
apparatus: BASS small flow duct inside the sealed Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), equipped with variable-speed fan (0.5 to 10.0 cm/s), gaseous N2 injection line, hot-wire igniters, multi-angle color video cameras, and radiometer sensors.
experimental_variables: Extinguishment outcome (Flow cessation vs. N2 dilution quenching)
